overview.headline: Glider glide angle and lift drag balance in steady descent

keyPoints.point: A glider is an aircraft with no engine that descends steadily after release
keyPoints.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyPoints.point: Steady descent holds constant velocity with no acceleration while losing altitude
keyPoints.quote: If a glider is in a steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent, it loses altitude as it travels.

keyPoints.point: Distance flown and altitude change determine glide angle using trigonometry
keyPoints.quote: If we know the distance flown and the altitude change, we can calculate the glide angle using trigonometry.

keyPoints.point: Lift and drag combine with glide angle to balance weight in steady flight
keyPoints.quote: The lift L times the cosine cos of the glide angle plus the drag D times the sine sin of the glide angle is equal to the weight W

keyTerms.gloss: aircraft with no engine that can glide
keyTerms.quote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.

keyTerms.gloss: angle where flight path meets ground
keyTerms.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio linking height change to distance flown
keyTerms.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force balanced with drag and weight
keyTerms.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.
